title: Atlas declarative adapter security assessment
scope: Strict declarative source mapping, record validation, change-triggered approval rules, SDK exports, atlas-provider CLI, and Cartographer lineage

approved_targets: Synthetic declarative adapter specifications and records
prohibited_actions: Use declarative adapters to bypass reviewed healthcare handling
Treat a mapping specification as authorization or compliance approval

actors: Atlas universal translator and approval engine
trust_boundaries: Bounded JSON specification into a registered IndustryAdapter
Untrusted source record into strict allowlisted field mapping
Canonical change set into declarative approval rules
Mapping evidence into Company Memory and Cartographer
data_flows: Allowlisted top-level JSON scalars into typed canonical attributes
Versioned observation into change intelligence and Cartographer
Matched rule into a proposal that remains subject to approval policy

threats.name: Unmapped data enters Company Memory
threats.control: Every source key must be an identity, timestamp, version, or declared mapping; unknown fields fail before storage.

threats.name: Specification hides ambiguous or duplicate configuration
threats.control: Specs are bounded to 64 KiB, reject duplicate JSON keys and unknown fields, require strict string and boolean types, and use schema version 1.

threats.name: Unsafe types or timestamps corrupt canonical state
threats.control: Values are scalar-only with strict booleans, bounded strings, finite decimals, bounded integers, and timezone-aware ISO 8601 timestamps.

threats.name: Generic mapping bypasses sensitive-data review
threats.control: Common direct-sensitive field names and healthcare, clinical, and medical domains are rejected and require a reviewed coded adapter.

threats.name: Declarative rule executes an action
threats.control: Rules create ActionProposal objects only; normal approval policy, separate execution queue, executor allowlist, exact confirmation, and receipts remain mandatory.

threats.name: CLI validation prints source values
threats.control: validate-record returns adapter identity, mapped field names, spec hash, and version presence only; errors are bounded and payload-free.

findings.finding: A synthetic two-version asset mapping reached Company Memory, change intelligence, two Cartographer cards, and three pending proposals.
Name-based sensitive-field exclusion reduces accidental intake but cannot classify the meaning of arbitrary custom field names or values.
Real source schemas require data inventory, retention, access, and domain review before use.

validation: Nine focused declarative adapter tests passed.
Synthetic records produced typed canonical observations, deterministic changes, Cartographer lineage, and approval-gated proposals.
Negative tests rejected unknown and sensitive fields, healthcare domain use, strict type failures, naive timestamps, non-finite decimals, duplicate keys, and oversized specs.
CLI scaffold, inspect, and payload-free validate-record paths passed.
Installed SDK smoke produced two observations, two Cartographer cards, and one pending declarative proposal without returning record values.
residual_risk: Field-name checks cannot detect sensitive values placed under misleading custom names.
Declarative rules are intentionally limited to single changed fields and do not replace reviewed domain policy.
No live source, credential, customer data, external action, or production deployment was used.
Recheck before enabling any real organization schema or expanding the operator set.
